when.quote: When a customer needs to file a dispute for a debit card transaction (unauthorized charges, ATM errors, merchant issues, or incorrect amounts), the agent must gather comprehensive information and follow Regulation E requirements.

starts.note:
customer: start only when the customer asks to dispute one or more debit card transactions. This includes a customer who, during a transaction review in another job, denies a transaction and agrees when the agent advises filing a dispute. Such reviews are a chip/CVV mismatch, a fraud alert, or the PIN lock investigation's check for successful unauthorized transactions on a card that cannot be unlocked.

File one dispute for each transaction the customer names. Card actions (a freeze, or a close and reissue) are not optional offers: they follow from the categories of the disputes actually filed, as the dispute procedure requires. A dispute held back by the open-dispute limit, or dropped by the customer after a record check, sets no card action.

If the customer opens by asking for a human agent, offer to help first, as the policy says, and transfer only on the 4th request.
starts.quote: When a customer needs to file a dispute for a debit card transaction (unauthorized charges, ATM errors, merchant issues, or incorrect amounts), the agent must gather comprehensive information and follow Regulation E requirements.

tools.not_used: Blocking future recurring charges is a separate job, block_recurring_payments. It runs after the disputes are filed, and only if the customer wants future charges stopped on a card that stays open (see recurring_block_followup). The block tool requires an ACTIVE card.
The credit card check after a lost or stolen debit card belongs to lost_stolen_card_cross_product_security_protocol (see cross_product_handoff).
Doc 005 is cited only for its list of account names by tier. A dispute never closes a checking account.

A fraud alert on a card with a denied transaction is never cleared; doc 003 clears an alert only when the customer confirms all transactions are legitimate. The card follows its card action instead (alert_card_no_clear).

Its own description limits credit_type to 'rebate_credit' for missing rebates and 'fee_refund' for incorrect fee charges. Dispute provisional credit is recorded only through the provisional_credit_eligible argument of file_debit_card_transaction_dispute_6281.

steps.do: Choose dispute_category from what went wrong: duplicate_charge for a duplicate; incorrect_amount for a charge higher than expected; goods_services_not_received for goods or services paid for and never received; recurring_charge_after_cancellation for a subscription or membership charged after cancellation; atm_cash_discrepancy for an ATM that dispensed the wrong amount or no cash; atm_deposit_not_credited for a deposit not credited. For a transaction the customer did not make, decide whether fraud is suspected: if yes, card_present_fraud for in-store/physical transactions (also when the customer still holds the card, e.g. a PIN purchase in another city or a cloned or skimmed card after a chip/CVV mismatch, and when someone else used a lost or stolen card or its PIN physically), card_not_present_fraud for online/phone or card-number-only transactions and for a person-to-person transfer (EveryonePay or similar; record type everyonepay) the customer did not make with no in-person card use; never unauthorized_transaction when fraud is suspected. Use unauthorized_transaction only when fraud is not suspected (e.g., a family member used the card without permission). card_present_fraud is a card used 'not by customer': if the charge came from the customer's own arrangement (e.g., an automatic recurring charge they set up), it is not card_present_fraud; ask the customer what went wrong with it and classify by that. If it is unclear whether fraud is suspected, ask; for example, fraud is suspected when the customer never made the purchase, still has the card, and the charge is somewhere they have not been.
steps.quote: Only use 'unauthorized_transaction' when fraud is NOT suspected (e.g., family member used card without permission, customer forgot about a transaction, etc.).

done_when:
All of the following hold:
- The customer is verified and the verification is logged (once per conversation; reused when the job comes from a transaction review or the PIN lock investigation).
- Every requested dispute that passes the pre-filing rules and fits the account's open-dispute limit has been filed with file_debit_card_transaction_dispute_6281, one per transaction_id, with its category, transaction type, discovery date, provisional-credit decision, liability cap and card_action. Existing open disputes, and disputes filed earlier in this conversation, were counted per account, and each dispute was filed and confirmed before the next.
- Where the customer's amount differed from the record, the customer was told the recorded amount; the dispute went on to filing or was not filed because the customer dropped it. A Rho-Bank ATM claim the record did not support was explained and filed only if the customer still wanted it.
- Any dispute held back by a rule, the limit, a failed match, or deposit records the customer accepted has been explained; a held-back or dropped dispute set no card action.
- Each card's most severe action among its filed disputes has been performed once, after the last dispute: a freeze; a closure with reason lost, stolen or fraud_suspected (plus a replacement if the customer wanted one and the tier allows it now, or the Entry-tier 48-hour wait after closure explained); or nothing for keep_active. A fraud alert on a card with a denied transaction was not cleared.
- If a closed card was lost or stolen, the cross-product credit card check has been handed off.
- The customer has a per-dispute summary of liability, provisional credit (immediate for a confirmed Rho-Bank ATM discrepancy), timelines, any affidavit and card status.
- A PIN-locked card with only declined attempts had no dispute filed; the customer was told no money was taken.
- If a call failed after a corrected retry, the failure has been explained and a transfer offered; a transfer on request happened only on the 4th request.
